result.summary: The food delivery home screen is largely well-composed: header, search bar, category chips, promo banner, carousels, and bottom nav all render correctly. The partially visible carousel item at the right edge ('Trattoria Piccol...') and the card cut off at the bottom of the viewport are expected scroll affordances and not defects. A few minor visual/accessibility refinements remain: low-contrast placeholder and secondary text, an unlabelled notification badge, and a favorite (heart) button that relies on icon-only affordance over busy imagery.

issues.description: The search field placeholder text 'Restaurants, dishes, groceries' is light gray on a light gray background, giving low contrast that may be hard to read for users with low vision.
issues.suggestion: Darken the placeholder color (e.g., to a mid-gray meeting 4.5:1 contrast against the field background) or increase the field/placeholder contrast.

issues.description: The notification bell in the top-right shows a red unread badge dot with no numeric count or visible label, so the meaning of the badge is ambiguous and icon-only for screen readers.
issues.suggestion: Provide an accessible label such as 'Notifications, unread items' and consider showing a count or tooltip explaining the badge.

issues.description: The heart (favorite) buttons on the 'Popular right now' cards are white outline icons on dark circular overlays; on the lighter pizza image the second heart's dark circle blends with the busy background, reducing tap-target visibility.
issues.suggestion: Ensure a consistent semi-opaque scrim behind the heart icon and add a visible pressed/filled state so the control reads clearly on all imagery.

issues.description: Delivery fee labels such as '€0.90 delivery' and '€2.40 delivery' use a light gray that is close to the page background, lowering legibility of pricing information.
issues.suggestion: Increase the text contrast of secondary pricing metadata to meet WCAG AA (4.5:1) against the background.
